scenario.name: NIST SP 800-86 & Microsoft DFIR — Event Log Clearing via wevtutil.exe & USN Journal Recovery (EID 1102 / 104)
scenario.overview: Picture a wide multi-lane city highway approaching an overhead exit sign gantry and a row of striped toll plaza booths with automated lifting barrier arms. Cruising down the multi-lane express highway, a driver mounts a cloned electronic toll transponder behind the windshield right before entering the fast-pass lane. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches. The highway authority’s overhead license-plate camera spots two different vehicles using the same toll pass minutes apart and sounds an immediate toll-plaza alert. In this scenario (T1070.001, NIST SP 800-86 & Microsoft DFIR, Event Log Clearing via wevtutil.exe & USN Journal Recovery , EID 1102 / 104), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mass Channel Enumeration, then immutable Audit Log Cleared Events, then nTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Mass Channel Enumeration, then Immutable Audit Log Cleared Events, then NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Mass Channel Enumeration & wevtutil.exe cl Execution (Sysmon EventID 1)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.001 - Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs)
stages.description: Cruising down the multi-lane express highway, a driver mounts a cloned electronic toll transponder behind the windshield right before entering the fast-pass lane. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the toll booth attendant go about their routine. To erase post-exploitation traces before disconnecting, the attacker runs cmd.exe /c "for /F %i in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%i"" or PowerShell Clear-EventLog.
